title: A Deep Learning System to Screen Novel Coronavirus Disease 2019 Pneumonia.
summary: The study distinguished COVID-19 from influenza-A viral pneumonia and healthy cases; overall accuracy was 86.7% on a held-out set of 90 CT cases (30 per category). The source reports 618 CT samples from three hospitals; 528 samples were used for training/validation and 90 were held out from patients not included in training. The test is an internal held-out sample, not an independent external cohort. Published abstract/full text do not establish clinical benefit or prospective utility.
ai_technology: A 3D deep-learning model segmented candidate infection regions; a location-attention classifier categorized CT regions and a Noisy-or Bayesian function combined confidence into a case-level prediction.
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

source_review.scope: The first located result-bearing version is the authors’ arXiv v1 dated 2020-02-21; its abstract reports the same 86.7% CT-case accuracy later reported in the journal article. The original full-text study is a specific retrospective diagnostic-validation question, eligible under the project criteria. Active/archived catalog searches found no same-cohort record; the active Mount Sinai COVID-CT entry is a different model, input set and cohort. A later Applied Intelligence article was retracted for reusing this study’s data/text and is treated as the same underlying work, not a separate discovery.
